Most commercial cleaning companies aren't struggling because they can't find leads. They're struggling because nothing happens after the first contact.

A prospect visits your website. Or you send a cold email and get a reply. And then — silence. No follow-up system. No consistent touchpoints. No structured way to move that interest into a booked conversation.

That's not a lead problem. That's a pipeline problem.

Here's what most cleaning company owners get wrong about cold email outreach: they treat it like a one-shot attempt. Send the email, wait for a reply, move on if nothing comes. But the data consistently shows that 80% of sales require five or more follow-ups. Most cleaning companies stop at one.

The companies winning recurring office cleaning contracts aren't necessarily sending more emails. They're running a system. A sequence that opens with a relevant, specific reason for reaching out. Follows up with proof — a case study, a result, a number. Sends a third touchpoint that makes it easy to say yes to a conversation, not a contract.

Trust is built through consistency, not volume.

A prospect who receives four or five well-timed, relevant messages from your company will remember you when their current cleaner lets them down — and they always do eventually. But only if you've stayed in front of them.
